messages:
Nora: hitting flaky CI on sample-app seed step. sometimes device-code login succeeds, other times it times out and we get duplicate device codes from multiple containers.

Evan: repro steps? sounds like parallel headless logins racing for the same profile token.

Nora: our docker-compose brings up 3 workers that run `/app/scripts/seed.sh` which calls `redwoodctl login --profile ci --headless` if no token exists. when multiple containers start simultaneously they all do the login flow; some calls fail with 409 or a timeout. intermittently one wins and others overwrite token with a stale state.

Julie: that aligns with the logs i saw: repeated device codes and device polling 403/410. we shouldn't be doing parallel interactive logins against the same profile in CI.

Nora: quick trimmed log: 
```
[worker-1] device code requested: code=ABCD1234
[worker-2] device code requested: code=WXYZ9876
[worker-1] polling -> 403 polling not authorized
[worker-3] polling -> 200 token saved
[worker-1] saving token -> file truncated
[worker-2] polling -> 410 expired
```

Evan: short-term workaround: have seed.sh create a lockfile in the mounted ci/redwood dir and only one container runs redwoodctl login. others wait or reuse token. e.g. `flock /tmp/redwood.lock -c 'redwoodctl login --profile ci --headless'`

Julie: long-term we should make redwoodctl behave better in multi-process environments: options:
- atomic write for token files (write tempfile + rename)
- advisory file lock while writing tokens
- return clearer exit codes for CI callers when a token was concurrently created (so callers can treat that as success)
- add `--ci-seed` mode that does idempotent login and is safe for parallel runs (acquires lock in REDWOOD_HOME)

Nora: i can draft a tiny patch to use atomic rename on token save. That should reduce truncation corruption. but it won't prevent duplicate device codes.

Evan: maybe also add an environment var `REDWOOD_LOGIN_LOCK=/path/to/lock` that CLI will use if present. CI runners can set that to a mounted path. Use case: compose mounts `./ci/redwood:/root/.redwood` and `./ci/locks:/var/locks` then `-e REDWOOD_LOGIN_LOCK=/var/locks/redwood.lock`.

Julie: agree. also update sample-app docker-compose to show `flock` example and set `REDWOOD_LOGIN_LOCK` in the compose file. docs should recommend not running multiple login flows concurrently.

devex-bot: created issue #3644: "redwoodctl: make headless login idempotent for parallel CI seeds" and assigned to @evan

ci-bot: queued job `devex/ci-login-race` to run on evan/parallel-login-fix branch

Nora: adding note to sample-app README and to onboarding checklist. thanks! :seedling:
